description: GO term definitions, Mdh2 molecular weight versus nuclear pore passive diffusion limit, and composition of the Gallina 2015 nuclear periphery annotation batch
code:
import requests, json
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
h={"User-Agent":"curation-agent/1.0","Accept":"application/json"}

# --- GO term definitions ---
for go in ["GO:0034399","GO:0005829","GO:0005634","GO:0005777","GO:0101031"]:
    r=requests.get(f"https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/{go}",headers=h,timeout=60).json()
    t=r["results"][0]
    print(f"{go}  {t['name']}")
    print("   def:", t.get("definition",{}).get("text"))

# --- MW / nuclear pore passive diffusion argument ---
MWaa=dict(A=71.08,R=156.19,N=114.10,D=115.09,C=103.14,E=129.12,Q=128.13,G=57.05,H=137.14,I=113.16,
L=113.16,K=128.17,M=131.19,F=147.18,P=97.12,S=87.08,T=101.10,W=186.21,Y=163.18,V=99.13)
seq=requests.get("https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P22133.json",headers=h,timeout=60).json()['sequence']['value']
mw=sum(MWaa[c] for c in seq)+18.02
print(f"\nMdh2 monomer MW = {mw/1000:.1f} kDa ; functional homodimer ~ {2*mw/1000:.1f} kDa")
print(f"Mdh2-GFP fusion monomer ~ {(mw+26900)/1000:.1f} kDa ; tagged dimer ~ {(2*(mw+26900))/1000:.1f} kDa")
print("NPC passive diffusion limit for globular proteins ~ 40 kDa")

# --- provenance figure: the Gallina-2015 nuclear-periphery batch ---
nm=pd.read_csv("gallina2015_nuclear_periphery_batch.csv")
nm['gene']=nm['gene'].fillna(nm['accession'])
cat={ 'CMR1':'INQ core / DNA damage','MRC1':'INQ core / DNA damage','PPH3':'INQ core / DNA damage',
 'HSP104':'Chaperone / aggregase','BTN2':'Chaperone / aggregase','APJ1':'Chaperone / aggregase',
 'MDH2':'Metabolic enzyme','GLN1':'Metabolic enzyme','QCR6':'Metabolic enzyme','DUG2':'Metabolic enzyme','Q12288':'Metabolic enzyme',
 'TUB1':'Cytoskeleton / cell wall','PIR1':'Cytoskeleton / cell wall','ARP6':'Cytoskeleton / cell wall'}
nm['class']=nm.gene.map(cat).fillna('Other nuclear / signalling')
print("\nComposition of the 28-protein 'nuclear periphery' batch from PMID:25817432")
print(nm['class'].value_counts().to_string())

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(11,5.2))
order=['INQ core / DNA damage','Chaperone / aggregase','Metabolic enzyme','Cytoskeleton / cell wall','Other nuclear / signalling']
cols=dict(zip(order,["#4C78A8","#72B7B2","#F58518","#E45756","#BAB0AC"]))
y=0; ticks=[]; labs=[]
for c in order:
    sub=nm[nm['class']==c].sort_values('gene')
    for _,r in sub.iterrows():
        ax.barh(y,1,color=cols[c]); ticks.append(y); labs.append(r.gene); y+=1
ax.set_yticks(ticks); ax.set_yticklabels(labs,fontsize=8)
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlabel("each bar = one gene product annotated GO:0034399 'nuclear periphery' (IDA) citing PMID:25817432")
handles=[plt.Rectangle((0,0),1,1,color=cols[c]) for c in order]
ax.legend(handles,order,loc="lower right",fontsize=8,frameon=True)
ax.set_title("All 28 'nuclear periphery' IDA annotations from Gallina 2015 come from one INQ\nstress-deposit set, which also contains Qcr6 (mitochondrial) and Pir1 (cell wall)",fontsize=11)
for lbl in ax.get_yticklabels():
    if lbl.get_text()=='MDH2': lbl.set_fontweight('bold'); lbl.set_color('#B3100A'); lbl.set_fontsize(10)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
